security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU emulates CHERI but fails to check ASR permission in PCC before executing MRET/SRET/DRET or allowing access to privileged/debug CSRs. The spec now explicitly requires ASR in PCC for: (a) MRET_CHERI, SRET_CHERI, DRET_CHERI execution, (b) all privileged CSR read/write access, (c) debug CSR access, (d) CBO_INVAL_CHERI execution. Omitting any of these checks means capability-restricted (sandboxed) guest code can escape its authority boundary by manipulating privileged state or executing xRET to escalate to a higher privilege level.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: MRET|SRET|DRET CSR_RW check_asr_pcc|ASR_PERM privileged_csr_access debug_csr_access helper_mret helper_sret csrrw csrrs csrrc riscv_csrrw
security_spec.summary: CHERI ASR permission scope clarified: MRET/SRET/DRET and all privileged/debug CSR access now require ASR in PCC — missing checks in QEMU TCG translate/helper code allows capability-sandboxed guest to escalate privilege or corrupt privileged state

findings.finding: CHERI is not implemented in this QEMU codebase. No PCC, ASR permission, MRET_CHERI/SRET_CHERI/DRET_CHERI, or CHERI-specific CSR access checks exist. The PR correctly adds the standard RISC-V menvcfg.CDE gate for scountinhibit access per Smcdeleg/Ssccfg spec — this is a security improvement, not a vulnerability. The scountinhibit_pred now properly raises illegal-instruction when menvcfg.CDE=0, preventing S-mode from accessing counter delegation features without M-mode authorization.

spec_citations.excerpt: #When menvcfg.CDE=0, attempts to access scountinhibit raise an illegal-instruction exception.#

findings.finding: Standard RISC-V SRET implementation with no CHERI awareness. Since CHERI is not implemented in this QEMU, there is no CHERI-specific vulnerability — the code correctly handles the non-cheri SRET path. If CHERI were to be added, this function would need ASR permission checks on PCC before writing the unsealed sepc_cheri to PCC, and the function name would need to become SRET_CHERI.

spec_citations.excerpt: An illegal instruction fault is raised when pcc does not grant asr_perm because MRET_CHERI and SRET_CHERI require access to privileged CSRs.

findings.finding: Standard RISC-V MRET implementation with no CHERI awareness. No CHERI vulnerability since CHERI is not implemented. If CHERI support is added, this must check ASR permission in PCC before executing MRET_CHERI to prevent sandboxed guest code from escalating privilege via xRET.

spec_citations.excerpt: An illegal instruction fault is raised when pcc does not grant asr_perm because MRET_CHERI and SRET_CHERI require access to privileged CSRs.

findings.finding: Standard CSR access check performs privilege and extension checks but has no CHERI ASR permission gate. Since CHERI is not implemented, this is not a vulnerability. If CHERI were added, all privileged CSR read/write paths would need to check PCC.ASR before granting access, otherwise sandboxed guest code could read/write privileged CSRs to escape its authority boundary.

spec_citations.excerpt: CSR*, MRET_CHERI, SRET_CHERI, CBO_INVAL_CHERI | Illegal instruction | pcc does not grant asr_perm when required for CSR access or execution of MRET_CHERI, SRET_CHERI or CBO_INVAL_CHERI

findings.finding: Standard MRET decode/translate. No CHERI-specific translation logic or ASR check at the TCG translation level. The gen_helper_mret helper is the standard non-CHERI version. Compliant because CHERI is not implemented.
Standard SRET decode/translate. No CHERI-specific logic. The gen_helper_sret call uses the standard non-CHERI helper. Compliant because CHERI is not implemented.

menvcfg write correctly includes MENVCFG_CDE in its writable mask (bit 60). The CDE bit is only writable when ext_smcdeleg is configured. The mask properly separates always-writable bits from extension-gated bits. No security issues.

                MENVCFG_CBZE | MENVCFG_CDE;
...

findings.finding: scountinhibit read properly masks mcountinhibit with mcounteren, ensuring S-mode only sees bits delegated by M-mode. Combined with the predicate now checking MENVCFG_CDE, this is correct and secure.

spec_citations.excerpt: Smcdeleg/Ssccfg defines a new scountinhibit register, a masked alias of mcountinhibit. For counters delegated to S-mode, the associated mcountinhibit bits can be accessed via scountinhibit.

findings.finding: scountinhibit write correctly constrains S-mode writes to mcounteren-delegated counter bits, forwarding to write_mcountinhibit. No privilege bypass possible through this path.
findings.snippet: return write_mcountinhibit(env, csrno, val & env->mcounteren, ra);
